Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

to err is human, to forgive divine phrase

also to err is human

classical

Cic. Phil. 12.5: cujusvīs hominis est errāre; nūllīus nisi īnsipientis in errōre persevērāre

Cujusvīs hominis est errāre.

Literally “it is any man’s part to err”; Cicero goes on, “but no one’s but a fool’s to persist in error”.

Other words

  • Errāre hūmānum est, ignōscere dīvīnum.

    also used · modern · Traupman 255

    The modern form of the saying. We have found no ancient source for it; its second half, ignōscere dīvīnum, answers the English.

See also forgive.

SourcesJohn C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.

Cicero, Philippics 12.5, checked against the Latin Library text (the Perseus text has persevērāre in errōre).
